dedupe_keys.name: daymet daily surface weather and climatology on a 1 km grid for north america hawaii and puerto rico ornl daac

description: Daymet is a research product of the Environmental Sciences Division at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), distributed by the NASA ORNL Distributed Active Archive Center (ORNL DAAC). It gives long-term, continuous, gridded estimates of daily weather by interpolating and extrapolating ground station observations with statistical modelling, to estimate near-surface conditions where no instruments exist. Coverage: daily minimum and maximum temperature, precipitation, vapour pressure, shortwave radiation, snow water equivalent and day length on a 1 km by 1 km grid over continental North America and Hawaii from 1980, and over Puerto Rico from 1950, through the end of the latest full calendar year; pre-derived climatological summaries and cross-validation files are also offered. Version 4 has been available since December 2020. Format and access: direct downloads with companion documentation from the ORNL DAAC, a THREDDS data server, 2 by 2 degree tiled subsets in netCDF, a Single Pixel Extraction Tool that returns a text table for any point, and RESTful web services for pixel and gridded subsets, with client libraries in several programming languages. Free; the site has a sign-in, but the download routes described did not state that one is required. Licence: not read. Caveats: the grids are interpolated from station data, so accuracy falls where stations are sparse; the model inputs are a digital elevation model, horizon files, a land-water mask and daily station temperature and precipitation. Simulation uses: long daily weather series for heat, cold, snow and precipitation exposure of infrastructure, demand modelling and climate adaptation studies in North America. Related records: GEFF-ERA5 (data-geff-era5-global-fire-danger-reanalysis) provides global fire weather indices from a reanalysis.
